table.caption: Population and household trash collected in one year in three towns (invented data for practice)

items.q: A town of 30,000 people uses 4,500,000 liters of water a day. How many liters is that per person per day?

mistakes.why: You divided people by liters. Per person means the total ÷ the number of people.
You multiplied. A per-person value divides the total by the population.

items.q: A family’s car used 1,200 liters of gasoline in 15,000 km of driving. Write the setup for the fuel used per km, with units, then give the answer.

mistakes.why: That gives km per liter. "Liters per km" puts liters on top: 1200 L / 15000 km.
That is km per liter (15000 / 1200). The question asks for liters per km.

items.q: Which value lets you compare how much water two cities of very different sizes use, fairly?
options: Water use per person
Total water use
Number of water pipes
Area of each city’s reservoir

why.correct: A bigger city uses more in total just because it has more people. Dividing by population gives a per-person rate you can compare.
options: Right: per capita removes the effect of size.
Totals depend mostly on how many people live there.
Pipe counts do not measure use.
Storage size does not measure use.

items.q: A lake’s water level drops 36 cm over 12 weeks of drought. What is the average rate of drop, in cm per week?

mistakes.why: You divided weeks by cm. A rate in cm per week puts cm on top.
You multiplied. A rate per week divides the change by the number of weeks.

items.q: A county of 2,500 square kilometers has 400,000 people. How many people live there per square kilometer?

mistakes.why: You divided area by people. Density is people ÷ area.

items.q: A school of 800 students throws away 2.4 metric tons of food each month. How many kilograms is that per student per month? (1 metric ton = 1,000 kg.)

why.correct: 2.4 metric tons = 2,400 kg. $\frac{2{,}400\,\text{kg}}{800\,\text{students}} = 3$ kg per student per month.

mistakes.why: That is metric tons per student. The question asks for kilograms: change 2.4 metric tons to 2,400 kg first.

items.q: A leaky faucet drips 15 mL every minute. Which setup gives the liters lost in one day?
options: 15 mL/min × 60 min/h × 24 h/day × 1 L/1,000 mL
15 mL/min × 60 min/h × 24 h/day × 1,000 mL/1 L
15 mL/min × 24 h/day × 1 L/1,000 mL

why.correct: Minutes per hour and hours per day turn a per-minute rate into a per-day rate; 1 L per 1,000 mL turns mL into L: 21.6 L a day.
options: Right: every unit cancels except L per day.
The last factor is upside down, so mL do not cancel and the number is a million times too big.
Dividing by time makes the rate smaller, not a daily total.
It skips the 60 minutes in an hour, so minutes and hours do not cancel.

items.q: How many metric tons of trash per person did Alder collect in the year?

units: metric tons per person per year

mistakes.why: You divided people by trash. Per person is the trash ÷ the people.

items.q: Which town produced the most trash per person?
options: Cedar
Birch
Alder
Alder and Birch tied

why.correct: Per person: Alder 0.5, Birch $\frac{20{,}000}{50{,}000} = 0.4$, Cedar $\frac{2{,}600}{4{,}000} = 0.65$ metric tons. Cedar is highest even though its total is lowest.
options: Right: 0.65 metric tons per person.
Birch has the largest total but 0.4 per person.
Alder is 0.5 per person.
Alder (0.5) and Birch (0.4) are not equal.

items.q: How many kilograms of trash per person did Birch collect? (1 metric ton = 1,000 kg.)

why.correct: $\frac{20{,}000\,\text{t}}{50{,}000\,\text{people}} = 0.4$ t per person; $0.4 \times 1{,}000 = 400$ kg per person.

mistakes.why: 0.4 is in metric tons. Multiply by 1,000 to get kilograms.

items.q: A newspaper headline says "Birch is the most wasteful town." What does the per-person data show?
options: Birch has the largest total but the smallest per-person amount.
Birch is the most wasteful by both measures.
Birch has the most trash per person.
The towns are too different in size to compare.

why.correct: Birch’s total (20,000 t) is largest because it has the most people; per person (0.4 t) it is the least wasteful of the three.
options: Right: totals reflect size; per person shows behavior.
Per person, Birch is the lowest.
Cedar has the most per person (0.65 t).
Per-person values make a fair comparison across sizes.

items.q: People in a city of 50,000 each use an average of 180 liters of water per day. How many liters does the whole city use in a day?

mistakes.why: You divided the population by the rate. A total is the rate times the number of people: 180 L/person × 50,000 people.

why.correct: $\frac{180\,\text{L}}{1\,\text{person}} \times 50{,}000\,\text{people} = 9{,}000{,}000$ L per day. People cancel, leaving liters.

items.q: A car drove 600 km on 40 liters of gasoline. What is its fuel use in kilometers per liter?
options: 15 km/L
560 km/L

why.correct: "Kilometers per liter" puts kilometers on top: 600 km / 40 L = 15 km/L.
options: That is 40 / 600, which is liters per kilometer. The question asks for kilometers per liter.
Right: the quantity after "per" goes on the bottom.
That is 600 × 40. "Per" means divide.
That is 600 - 40. A rate is a division, not a difference.

items.q: A forest covered 5,200 hectares in 2010 and 4,600 hectares in 2022. What was the average rate of forest loss, in hectares per year?

mistakes.why: 600 ha is the total loss. Divide by the 12 years to get the loss per year.
You divided the 2022 area by 12. A rate of change is the change (5,200 - 4,600) divided by the time.

why.correct: Change: 5,200 ha - 4,600 ha = 600 ha lost. Time: 2022 - 2010 = 12 years. Rate: 600 ha / 12 yr = 50 ha per year.

items.q: A landfill has 600,000 cubic meters of space left. It fills at a rate of 40,000 cubic meters per year. How many years until it is full?

mistakes.why: You multiplied. Divide the space by the rate so that cubic meters cancel and years are left.
You divided the rate by the space. Space ÷ rate gives years.

why.correct: $600{,}000\,\text{m}^{3} \div \frac{40{,}000\,\text{m}^{3}}{1\,\text{yr}} = 15$ years. Cubic meters cancel, leaving years.

items.q: Over ten years a city’s total water use rose 10% while its population rose 25%. What happened to water use per person?
options: It rose 35%
It rose 15%
It fell by about 12%
It stayed the same

why.correct: Per person means total ÷ people. The total became 1.10 times as large and the population 1.25 times as large, so the per-person use became 1.10 / 1.25 = 0.88 times as large: about 12% lower.
options: Adding the two percents treats both as increases in use. More people sharing the water lowers the per-person value.
The population grew faster than the total, so each person’s share shrank.
Right: the bottom of the fraction grew faster than the top.
It would stay the same only if the total and the population rose by the same percent.
